[heading=terms and definitions]
== Terms related to semantics and profiles

[[dpp-0086]]
=== interoperability

ability of two or more systems or applications to exchange information and to mutually use the information that has been exchanged

NOTE: Regional variant: the definition recorded from the merged concept pair was: capability of two or more entities to exchange items in accordance with a set of rules and mechanisms implemented by an interface in each entity, in order to perform their specified tasks

[.source]
<<ISOIEC22123,clause="3.6.1">>, <<EN18223,clause="3.1">>, similar, <<ISO18435,clause="3.12">>, similar, <<EN18219,clause="3.1.7">>



[[dpp-0088]]
=== semantic interoperability

ability for data shared by systems to be understood at the level of fully defined domain concepts

[.source]
<<ISO18308,clause="3.45">>, <<EN18223,clause="3.2">>



[[dpp-0089]]
=== technical interoperability

ability that covers the applications and infrastructures linking systems and services

[.source]
<<EN18223,clause="3.3">>



[[dpp-0090]]
=== application programming interface

set of methods ({{method}}) provided by an application component for use by other application components

[.source]
<<EN18222,clause="3.1">>



[[dpp-0091]]
=== representational state transfer application programming interface

service that allows for interaction with resources via a stateless, client-server architecture, typically using standard HTTP calls like GET, POST, PUT, and DELETE to perform methods ({{method}}) by an application component on these resources

[.source]
<<EN18222,clause="3.1.1">>



[[dpp-0092]]
=== method

particular way used to perform a specific action on a resource

[example]
--
read a DPP
--

[.source]
<<EN18222,clause="3.3">>



[[dpp-0093]]
=== parameter

data provided by a client, that is needed to perform a method ({{method}})

[example]
--
DPP ID for read DPP
--

[.source]
<<EN18222,clause="3.4">>



[[dpp-0094]]
=== result

return value after the execution of a method ({{method}})

[example]
--
the DPP
--

[.source]
<<EN18222,clause="3.5">>



[[dpp-0095]]
=== data exchange

storing, accessing, transferring, and archiving of data

[.source]
<<ISO15531,clause="3.1.5">>, <<EN18216,clause="3.2">>



[[dpp-0096]]
=== application

software functional element specific to the solution of a problem in industrial-process measurement and control

NOTE: An application can be distributed among resources and may communicate with other applications.

[.source]
<<IECTR62390,clause="3.1.2">>, <<IDTA01001,clause="1.1.2">>



[[dpp-0097]]
=== asset

entity owned by or under the custodial duties of an organization, which has either a perceived or actual value to the organization

NOTE: An asset can be single entity, a collection of entities, an assembly of entities or a composition of entities.

[example]
--
Examples for physical entities are equipment, raw material, parts components and pieces, supplies, consumables, physical products, and waste.
--

[example]
--
Software is an example of a digital asset.
--

[example]
--
A software license is an example of an intangible asset.
--

[.source]
<<IEC63278>>, modified, <<IDTA01001,clause="1.1.3">>



[[dpp-0098]]
=== attribute

data element of a property, a relation, or a class in information technology

[.source]
<<IEC63278>>, <<IDTA01001,clause="1.1.4">>



[[dpp-0099]]
=== Asset Administration Shell

standardized digital representation of an asset

NOTE: Asset Administration Shell and Administration Shell are used synonymously.

[.source]
<<IEC63278>>, modified, <<IDTA01001,clause="1.1.5">>



[[dpp-0100]]
=== class

description of a set of objects that share the same attributes, operations, methods, relationships, and semantics

[.source]
<<IECTR62390,clause="3.1.4">>, <<IDTA01001,clause="1.1.6">>



[[dpp-0101]]
=== capability

implementation-independent potential of a component to achieve an effect within a domain

NOTE: Capabilities can be orchestrated and structured hierarchically.

NOTE: Capabilities can be made executable via services.

NOTE: The impact manifests itself in a measurable effect within the physical world.

[.source]
<<I40GLOSS>>, modified, <<IDTA01001,clause="1.1.7">>



[[dpp-0102]]
=== coded value

value that can be looked up in a dictionary and can be translated

[.source]
<<ECLASS>>, <<IDTA01001,clause="1.1.8">>



[[dpp-0103]]
=== component

product used as a constituent in an assembled product, system, or plant

[.source]
<<IEC63278,clause="3.6">>, <<IDTA01001,clause="1.1.9">>



[[dpp-0104]]
=== concept

unit of knowledge created by a unique combination of characteristics

[.source]
<<IEC63278>>, <<IDTA01001,clause="1.1.10">>



[[dpp-0105]]
=== digital representation

information and services representing an entity from a given viewpoint

[example]
--
Examples of information are properties (e.g. maximum temperature), actual parameters (e.g. actual velocity), events (e.g. notification of status change), schematics (electrical), and visualization information (2D and 3D drawings).
--

[example]
--
Examples of services are asset services (for example providing the history of the configuration data or providing the actual velocity) and asset related services (for example providing a simulation).
--

[example]
--
Examples of viewpoints are mechanical, electrical, or commercial characteristics.
--

[.source]
<<IEC63278>>, modified, <<IDTA01001,clause="1.1.11">>



[[dpp-0106]]
=== digital twin

digital representation, sufficient to meet the requirements of a set of use cases

NOTE: In this context, the entity in the definition of digital representation is typically an asset.

[.source]
<<IDTA01001,clause="1.1.12">>



[[dpp-0107]]
=== explicit value

commonly used concept, like numbers (e.g. 109, 25) which do not need lookup in dictionaries

[.source]
<<ECLASS>>, <<IDTA01001,clause="1.1.13">>



[[dpp-0108]]
=== instance

concrete, clearly identifiable component of a certain type

NOTE: An individual entity of a type, for example a device, is obtained by defining specific property values.

NOTE: In an object-oriented view, an instance denotes an object of a class (of a type).

[.source]
<<IEC62890>>, modified, <<IDTA01001,clause="1.1.15">>



[[dpp-0109]]
=== instance asset

specific asset that is uniquely identifiable

[example]
--
Examples of instance assets are material, a product, a part, a device, a machine, software, a control system, or a production system.
--

[.source]
<<IEC63278>>, modified, <<IDTA01001,clause="1.1.16">>



[[dpp-0110]]
=== operation

executable realization of a function

NOTE: The term method is synonymous to operation.

NOTE: An operation has a name and a list of parameters [ISO 19119:2005, 4.1.3].

[.source]
<<I40GLOSS>>, modified, <<IDTA01001,clause="1.1.17">>



[[dpp-0111]]
=== property

defined characteristic suitable for the description and differentiation of products or components

NOTE: The concept of type and instance applies to properties.

NOTE: This definition applies to properties as described in IEC 61360/ ISO 13584-42.

NOTE: The property types are defined in dictionaries (like IEC component data dictionary or ECLASS), they do not have a value. The property type is also called data element type in some standards.

NOTE: The property instances have a value and are provided by the manufacturers. A property instance is also called property-value pair in certain standards.

NOTE: Properties include nominal value, actual value, runtime variables, measurement values, etc.

NOTE: A property describes one characteristic of a given object.

NOTE: The specification of a property can include predefined choices of values.

[.source]
<<I40GLOSS>>, modified, <<IDTA01001,clause="1.1.18">>



[[dpp-0112]]
=== qualifier

well-defined element associated with a property instance or SubmodelElement, restricting the value statement to a certain period of time or use case

NOTE: Qualifiers can have associated values.

[.source]
<<IEC62569>>, <<IDTA01001,clause="1.1.19">>



[[dpp-0113]]
=== service

distinct part of the functionality that is provided by an entity through interfaces

[.source]
<<IEC63278,clause="741-01-28">>, <<IDTA01001,clause="1.1.20">>



[[dpp-0114]]
=== Submodel

representation of an aspect of an asset

[.source]
<<IEC63278>>, <<IDTA01001,clause="1.1.21">>



[[dpp-0115]]
=== SubmodelElement

element of a Submodel

[.source]
<<IEC63278>>, <<IDTA01001,clause="1.1.22">>



[[dpp-0116]]
=== Submodel template

template for the representation of an aspect of an asset

[.source]
<<IEC63278>>, <<IDTA01001,clause="1.1.23">>



[[dpp-0117]]
=== Submodel template element

element of a Submodel template

[.source]
<<IEC63278>>, <<IDTA01001,clause="1.1.24">>



[[dpp-0118]]
=== system

interacting, interrelated, or interdependent elements forming a complex whole

[.source]
<<IEC63278,clause="3.2.123">>, <<IDTA01001,clause="1.1.25">>



[[dpp-0119]]
=== template

specification of the common features of an object in sufficient detail that such object can be instantiated using it

NOTE: Object can be anything that has a type.

[.source]
<<ISOIEC10746>>, <<IDTA01001,clause="1.1.26">>



[[dpp-0120]]
=== type

hardware or software element which specifies the common attributes shared by all instances of the type

[.source]
<<IECTR62390,clause="3.1.25">>, <<IDTA01001,clause="1.1.27">>



[[dpp-0121]]
=== type asset

(abstract) representation of a set of instance assets with common characteristics and features

NOTE: The set of instance assets may exist or may not exist.

[example]
--
Examples of type assets are type of material, a product type, a type of a part, a device type, a machine type, a type of software, a type of control system, a type of production system.
--

[.source]
<<IEC63278>>, <<IDTA01001,clause="1.1.28">>



[[dpp-0122]]
=== variable

software entity that may take different values, one at a time

[.source]
<<IEC61499>>, <<IDTA01001,clause="1.1.29">>
